speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry what is the impact of the current protectionist measures by the United States and China on Singapore's economy in relation to trade, investments, jobs and Singaporean workers who are working in companies which are or may be impacted by those measures.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Nonetheless, we are closely monitoring developments, particularly for any longer-term indirect impact on companies and workers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our economic agencies are in close contact with companies that may be affected.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Any disruption to global trade flows or trade volumes will affect big and small economies alike.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We hope that countries will exercise restraint and avoid further escalation of tensions.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I wish to thank the Minister for his reply.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Recently, I spoke to a professionals, managers and executives (PMEs) who work in a US multinational corporation (MNC) situated in China, and she has expressed concerns over the uncertainties of what is happening.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: There are a few things that are happening.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: They are looking at a potential review of the US interest rates, they are also looking at Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) coming up and, of course, at the same time, in the US, corporate taxes have gone down as well.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: So, there are quite a few measures which have caused a bit of uncertainty among workers, particularly so because there are quite a number of our PMEs and workers as well working in US MNCs or even Chinese MNCs in Singapore as well as their respective countries.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: So, I would urge the Government, especially the economic agencies, to pay a close watch and to stand prepared, particularly with measures, to help these workers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If I may just elaborate on some of those observations.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, any unilateral actions will have direct and indirect impact.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: All these, cumulatively, will cause a lot of uncertainties to the market.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There are uncertainties that are of immediate consequence because the trade flows and trade patterns are disrupted.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There are also indirect impacts that affect the longer-term investments and these create another round of uncertainties.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First and foremost, as an economy, we are an open economy.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We must make sure that we are not overly dependent on any particular markets, which is why a couple of days ago, I mentioned during the Debate on the President's Address that we must continually expand and diversify our markets to make sure that we are not overly dependent on any particular market for our products and investments.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This will require further study because there are at least a few levels of implications for us.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It requires us to watch the trends carefully, as Mr Patrick Tay has mentioned.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It requires us to review our economic models to make sure that we understand the shifts in the trade flows and ask ourselves what other actions do we need to undertake in order to safeguard ourselves from all these uncertainties.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, these are the things that MTI will continue to watch carefully, not just in isolation, but also with the other Government agencies and also with our other partners, trade partners included.
